title: Access
summary: DJDL's one Access page: who gets a license automatically (Nobody, Everyone who signs in, or Rules by identity provider group, verified email domain or claim, each giving a tier or an add-on), the Anonymous devices tier, Discover visibility, and the gates on update checks, app downloads, packs and packages as one matrix in one vocabulary, with a readiness error on a rule that can't match, Check a person, and one unsaved change (App downloads Customers → Public) in the save bar.
compare: Wide (.page.columns): Anonymous devices and Discover sit in the 400px aside; below 1600 they are two cards side by side under Automatic licenses; phone one column.
Automatic licenses: the heading alone, no subtitle; three choices (Nobody, Everyone who signs in, Rules: chosen).

Rules table: When · Gets · Label people see · Accounts · ⋯. Group studio-pro (Studio, 38), Group members (Standard, 412), Verified email domain example.edu (Education, 57), Claim vpnAccess is true (Polaris VPN, 'Add-on', ⚠ 0) with its readiness error under it ('This rule can’t match' / 'Pocket ID doesn’t send vpnAccess. Add it to Pocket ID’s claim map.', Open Connections), and the shaded fallback Everyone else who signs in (Trial, 143).
Anonymous devices: They get Free, '1 device · 2 decks · no recording'.
Discover: Hidden, People who can get it (chosen: 'Anyone a rule covers' and 'Adding DJDL issues their license', one line each), Everyone signed in.

Updates, downloads and packages: a legend band (Public, Signed in 'With or without a license.', Customers, Holds an entitlement), then rows with the same four-option matrix (App downloads' line is key.plrs.im/djdl; Stem separation models' 412 MB · on first use; npm @djdl's djdl-mapping-kit on pkg.plrs.im): Update checks (Customers), App downloads marked with 'was Customers' (Public), Packs (Stem separation models: Holds stems; Controller mappings: Public), Packages (npm @djdl: Public; Signed in and Entitlement don't apply).

Check a person ('Includes unsaved changes'): email (verified), groups, claims; the result 'Dana gets Education, plus Polaris VPN' from example.edu and claim vpnAccess, and a tick or cross per gate (Stem separation models: 'Education doesn’t include stems'), App downloads 'Public · unsaved'.
Save bar at the page's end (pinned while dirty in the built screen): '1 change: App downloads goes Public, so anyone can download DJDL 4.2.0 without signing in.' with Discard and Save access.
Phone: rules flow under their title, each matrix goes two by two, Check a person stacks.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.

In a full-page shot the save bar docks after the content, so the catch-all 'Everyone else who signs in → Trial' row is never hidden; DJDL's icon is the masthead tile; no numbers on sections (admin-1-24).

designReview.reviewer: Spacing and content pass against the products.overview and products.home references, all four sizes in both themes
designReview.verdict: Spacing and content pass: kit table, item rows, segmented matrix, card split and save bar; wide uses the aside; 0 screen spacing.

findings.issue: 40 spacing declarations: a div-grid rules table, custom gate rows and legend, verdict list and a sticky save bar drawn mid-page.
findings.resolution: Kit only: .table.stack-phone.flow with tr.note-row and tr.shaded, .choices.cols-3, .item-row with .segmented.matrix and .rows-label, .card-split, .icon-list, .save-bar, .page.columns with an .aside grid.

findings.issue: The subtitle narrated the page; card descriptions restated titles; 'can't match' was said in the count and the callout; the verdict note repeated the rule's error.
Desktop was a 2,350px single column while wide and tablet reflowed into a rail.
findings.resolution: Rail from 1280px (.page.columns.rail-360): Anonymous devices, Discover and Check a person in a 360px sticky column (.rail-cards, align-items start) beside Updates, downloads and packages. The rules table spans the full width above, because at 744px beside a rail its 'Label people see' column wrapped to three lines.

findings.issue: Fourth audience segment ellipsized ('Entitlement…') at every size.
findings.resolution: Label is 'Entitlement' and the matrix is content-width (.segmented.matrix.fit, 88px minimum, never ellipsized); on phone a 2x2 grid with 44px cells and a filled selected state.

findings.issue: The unsaved change was stated four times; subtitles restated titles.
findings.resolution: Subtitles on Anonymous devices and Discover removed; 'Public · unsaved' is 'Public'; the save bar says '1 change: App downloads goes Public.'; the row bar, 'was Customers' and the save bar stay; the tier-wins footer stays once.

findings.issue: Card heads varied (56 and 72); the save bar was only reachable at the end of a long page.
findings.resolution: Heads are .card-head.h56 (72 with a subtitle); the save bar is drawn pinned (.save-bar.pinned: lifted, with the safe-area inset) spanning the page. The warning callout already starts at the row text's x, so it was left. A sticky bar would overlay full-page captures, so the built screen does the pinning.

findings.issue: Delete the four-audience legend or turn it into tooltips; collapse Check a person to a closed disclosure.
findings.resolution: declined: The legend explains the segment meanings on first use and tooltips are invisible on touch; collapsing hides a core feature. Check a person moved into the rail instead.

findings.issue: Change the Save access button colour to the licence lime, or drop it to 'Entitled' wording everywhere.
findings.resolution: declined: Purple is the Access service accent; the kit's colours do not change in a spacing pass.
